items.question: Your fintech startup must keep Indian customer data in India. How do Regions affect your architecture?
items.answer: Deploy primary workloads in ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Regions are isolated — data stays in that partition unless you explicitly replicate out. Enable only required services in that Region, use KMS keys in ap-south-1, and audit cross-Region snapshots or S3 replication rules. DR in another Region requires legal review because replication moves data across borders.
followUps: What is an opt-in Region and when would you enable one?
How do AWS Control Tower guardrails enforce Region restrictions?
items.sixtySeconds: Region = residency boundary. ap-south-1 for India data. No cross-Region replication without compliance sign-off. KMS and backups stay in-Region.

items.question: An RDS instance in one Availability Zone fails during a data center outage. What should have been in place?
items.answer: Multi-AZ deployment with automatic failover to a standby in another AZ. Single-AZ RDS dies with the AZ. Application tier should also span AZs behind an Application Load Balancer with targets in at least two subnets in different AZs. Route 53 health checks alone cannot fix a database stuck in one AZ.
followUps: Does Multi-AZ mean read replicas in other AZs?
How long does RDS Multi-AZ failover typically take?
items.sixtySeconds: Multi-AZ RDS for AZ failure. ALB across AZ subnets. Single-AZ is a ticking bomb for production.

items.question: Why put CloudFront in front of S3 static assets instead of serving directly from the Region?
items.answer: Edge PoPs cache objects near users — latency drops from hundreds of ms to tens. Origin load shrinks because cache hits never reach S3. You can lock the bucket private with Origin Access Control. Regional Edge Caches absorb traffic between PoPs and origin. Direct S3 website hosting exposes the Region endpoint globally and lacks edge TLS termination options.
followUps: What is the difference between a PoP and a Regional Edge Cache?
items.sixtySeconds: CloudFront = edge cache + private S3. PoPs near users. Regional Edge Cache mid-tier. Fewer origin requests, lower latency.

items.question: When would you choose a Local Zone over deploying in the parent Region?
items.answer: When single-digit millisecond latency to a specific metro matters — live video, real-time bidding, gaming, or hybrid migration from on-premises in that city. Local Zones are extensions of a parent Region: same APIs, VPC can stretch with a Local Zone subnet. They cost more and have fewer instance types. Default Region deployment is fine for most web APIs.
followUps: How does Wavelength differ from a Local Zone?
Can you run an entire production stack only in a Local Zone?
items.sixtySeconds: Local Zone for metro ultra-low latency. Extension of parent Region. Not a full Region replacement — limited SKUs, higher cost.

items.question: You need global users with lowest latency and DR if ap-south-1 fails. Sketch the routing layer.
items.answer: Route 53 latency-based or geolocation routing to regional Application Load Balancers in ap-south-1 and a warm standby Region (e.g. ap-southeast-1). Health checks fail over DNS to the secondary. CloudFront caches static assets at edge globally. Active-active databases are hard — use warm standby with controlled failover or Aurora Global Database for managed cross-Region replication with RPO tradeoffs.
followUps: What is the difference between failover and latency routing policies?
How does Route 53 health check evaluate an ALB?
items.sixtySeconds: Route 53 latency + health checks. CloudFront for static. Warm standby Region for DR. Active-active DB is rare — know RPO/RTO.

items.question: A candidate says 'we picked us-east-1 because it is cheapest.' What is missing from that answer?
items.answer: Region choice is multi-dimensional: compliance and data residency, latency to primary users, service availability (some features launch in us-east-1 first but others are Region-specific), disaster recovery pairing, and operational timezone. Price alone ignores 200 ms RTT for Mumbai users and may violate residency. Strong answer: filter compliance and latency first, then compare price and service parity.
followUps: How do you measure latency from user populations to candidate Regions?
What is the impact of cross-Region data transfer pricing?
items.sixtySeconds: Never Region-shop on price alone. Compliance, latency, services, DR — then cost. us-east-1 is not universal default for global products.

items.question: Compare AWS global infrastructure to a typical on-premises single data center HA design.
items.answer: On-prem HA often means dual racks or dual sites you own — capital expense and fixed capacity. AWS HA maps to multi-AZ within a Region (like dual halls) plus optional multi-Region DR. Edge caching has no on-prem equivalent unless you operate a CDN. Elastic capacity replaces forecasting hardware. C# ASP.NET Core on EC2 follows the same AZ-spread rules as Java or Node — the platform is AZ-aware, not language-specific.
followUps: How does Azure Availability Zones compare conceptually?
When is hybrid with Direct Connect still needed?
items.sixtySeconds: On-prem dual site vs AWS multi-AZ + optional multi-Region. Edge = CDN you do not build. Language agnostic — spread tiers across AZs.
